title: Indistinguishable error conditions in state check
description:
File: oscore/src/edhoc/initiator.rs:265-266

Issue: `if self.state.lifecycle != Lifecycle::Message1Created || self.eph_secret.is_none()` returns the same `InvalidState` error for two distinct failure modes:
1. Wrong lifecycle (called out of order)
2. Ephemeral secret already consumed (called twice)

Impact: Debugging protocol errors becomes harder since the error doesn't indicate which condition failed.

Suggested fix: Return distinct errors or log which condition failed:
```rust
if self.state.lifecycle != Lifecycle::Message1Created {
    return Err(EdhocError::WrongLifecycle);  // new variant
}
if self.eph_secret.is_none() {
    return Err(EdhocError::EphemeralConsumed);  // new variant
}
```

Alternatively, keep single error but document in error message which sub-condition.

The local 13k+ line OSCORE/EDHOC implementation was replaced with the external `oscore` crate from crates.io. The issue about indistinguishable error conditions no longer applies since the code no longer exists in this project.
